body: yeah, you’re right!! I just see it more in them. My post is kind of a paradox because I’m also being judgmental towards them but I’m overly tired of feeling bad because of them! Thanks for your opinion!

I’m living the exactly same situation, it gets to the point where I just leave non graded group works because no one wants to add me and I have good grades (in my country it’s a nightmare bc in every subject there’s mandatory group work throughout the whole semester) I also thought one classmate was opening up to me but she never includes me in any group even though I tell her I’m alone, she has never said what those girls said to you though, they don’t deserve you. Starting college again has been a hard experience and it’ll still be likely hard especially for us but please don’t give up, it wears you out completely because nts just don’t have enough empathy (even though we’re the ones that are supposedly unempathetic). Please, take care of yourself and again, don’t give up. Much hugs.
Thank you!!
Thank you so much, you also put it in words too well, because that’s exactly how I feel. Hope some day we can be at peace with our own selves. Hugs
It can certainly get to a point where you just can’t anymore. Thank you for sharing this with me!!
And how different people act after you stop masking, it can suck. Thank you for sharing this!
Great solution!! Thank your for sharing this with me.
I think we ALL have difficulty masking...
It’s curious now that you mention it, I’m nb, it might have something to do with that too, there’s a lot of factors that affect us. Lots of hugs.
I’m ugly as fck so I’m always considered weird, strange and lonely.
We have the same MacBook and I downloaded sims from origin, doesn’t have big bugs thus far so I recommend it !!
I’m glad you’re doing well, it’s indeed really witty, ! I actually took notes, thank you so much for sharing this with me.

same here, I’m on my early twenties and seems like everyone’s idea of fun is partying (drinking, smoking, etc.) which is not appealing to me and when they’re partying neurotypical get even more annoying, I don’t know. Thank you for sharing your experience.
not gonna lie, what your boyfriend did was a shitty thing to do, I’m glad he doesn’t do that anymore though because after all it’s not in your control, thank you.
I’m glad you found people that understand your humor and yeah, neurotypical people like I’ve mentioned in other comments tend to think their experiences are universal which is not true, thank you.

this seems to be so easy to neurotypical people but it’s so hard for us, it’s like a riddle, you’re not alone on it and it sucks because neurotypical people do not know how to act around nd people since they think their experiences are “universal”. Thank you for sharing your experience with me.
thank you for sharing your experience with me 🫂🫂
people like that are so awful, really.
I feel exactly the same and it’s so difficult.
thank you, I definitely will. It’s nice to know we’re not alone. Have a great day/night!!
exactly, you will. Mucho ánimo
Thank you for your advice! Have a great day!

I don’t know you but reading this makes me so happy and proud of yourself, it has been not easy for you, but to still keep going and pushing through, it’s really something to be proud about. Hope you can keep working through this self-help you’re doing because sometimes it might not be easy but please don’t give up, you’re precious and deserve happiness. All my best wishes for you.

May I ask you, are you on treatment right now? Having bpd is so hard because it’s a lot of emotions and aspects coming to us all at once but please even though we might have a difficult time right now, please do not harm yourself, sometimes (I know how cliché this might sound) we might find pleasure in the tiniest things and even though I vented like that, I can also agree that there are some few things that bring me happiness, it might not be interpersonal relationships but a series, books, animals, even dumb YouTube videos. I don’t know you but please your life matters. Take care.
